laws.rule: On Iriomote, five restricted nature fields have daily visitor caps and need advance permission; some routes also need a registered guide. The island-wide figure of 1,200 visitors a day is a management-plan target, not a hard limit.
laws.heading: Iriomote ecotourism field usage system

laws.rule: Okinawa Prefecture accommodation tax starts on 1 February 2027: 2% of the room-only rate a person a night (the rate is rounded down to the JPY 1,000, and the tax is capped at JPY 2,000, about A$18.05, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82). Where a municipality also taxes (the prefecture names Motobu, Onna, Chatan, Miyakojima, Ishigaki and Nago as planning to), the 2% splits 0.8% prefecture and 1.2% municipality. Covers hotels, ryokan, simple lodgings and minpaku.
laws.heading: 沖縄県宿泊税条例 (in force 1 February 2027)

laws.rule: Okinawa Youth Protection and Development Ordinance (沖縄県青少年保護育成条例), art. 9. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 10 pm to 4 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) be out alone in that period without a proper reason. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.
laws.heading: 沖縄県青少年保護育成条例 (Okinawa), curfew for young people

laws.rule: Flying a drone (無人航空機) in a prefectural urban park (県営都市公園) is banned in principle. If use is unavoidable, send the papers to the park's management office and agree the use with it first. The page lists offices for Nago Chuo, the Okinawa Comprehensive Sports Park, Nakagusuku, Urasoe Odaira, Shuri Castle, Ounoyama, Kaigungo, the Peace Memorial Park and Banna. No penalty is stated on the page. Yen at A$1 = JPY 110.82 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
laws.heading: 沖縄県都市公園における無人航空機（ドローン等）の使用 (page updated 28 May 2026)

laws.rule: Naha City: 那覇市ごみのポイ捨て防止による環境美化促進条例 (Naha Ordinance on Promoting a Clean Environment by Preventing Litter, in force 9 January 1996). In the "beautification priority zone" of Kokusai-dori and Okiei-dori, dropping cigarette ends, bottles, wrappers, containers or cans can bring an administrative fine (過料) of up to JPY 10,000 (about A$90, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82). City page updated 2 April 2026. Naha's street-smoking rules for Kokusai-dori were not confirmed: the city page that describes them did not load (expired security certificate).

sites.name: Sēfa-utaki
sites.era: Ryukyu Kingdom sacred site, 15th century onward
sites.what: The Ryukyu Kingdom's most sacred place of worship, a rock and forest sanctuary in Nanjo (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.tickets: Adults (16+) JPY 600 (about AUD 5, RBA rate 30 October 2026), ages 7 to 15 JPY 300.
access.closures: Closed six days a year on lunar-calendar ritual days (lunar 1 to 3 May and 1 to 3 October; 9 to 11 November in 2026). From 2 November 2026 to 5 January 2027, access beyond the Ujo-guchi entrance is restricted and entry is free.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Sefa-utaki is a sacred prayer site: dress with as little exposed skin as possible. Avoid photography where you can, and especially don't photograph people with a prayer site behind them, as it means turning your back on the sacred area. No food or drink inside. No wheelchairs or prams (slippery stone paths).
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Sefa-utaki, the Ryukyu Kingdom's most sacred site, closes six days a year for quiet and conservation (lunar 1 to 3 May and 1 to 3 October; next 9 to 11 November 2026, then 5 to 7 June 2027). From 2 November 2026 to 5 January 2027 access stops at Ujo-guchi and admission is waived. Normal admission JPY 600 adults (about A$5.41 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026), open to anyone regardless of religion, nationality or gender.
culture-and-protocol.note: Sefa-utaki only, from its official site.

festivals.what: Naha Otsunahiki (Naha Great Tug-of-War) festival: October, with dates announced each year by Naha City; 2026 was 10 to 12 October, with the hatagashira banner parade on Kokusai-dori and the tug-of-war at Kumoji crossing (Route 58) on Sunday 11 October.

Okinawa all-war-dead memorial ceremony (沖縄全戦没者追悼式), held at Peace Memorial Park in Itoman on Irei no Hi each year. The official 2026 ceremony was on 23 June 2026 (Tuesday), 11:50 to 12:50, in the ceremonial plaza. 2027 start and finish times were not in the pages read this pass.

protocol_notes: The official 2026 memorial-ceremony Q&A says anyone may attend without a reservation. On the 2026 ceremony day, visitors to the ceremonial area went through metal-detector, baggage and drinks checks; lighters, blades and alcohol were taken at the entrance and not returned. General vehicles were kept out of the park from 8:30 to about 14:00, and park parking was not available. Drone flight in the park was prohibited that day under the Okinawa Prefecture Urban Park Ordinance. These were the 2026 official conditions; confirm the current year's guidance before travelling.
public_holidays: 2027-06-23: Irei no Hi (慰霊の日). Okinawa Prefecture sets 23 June as Irei no Hi by ordinance (Ordinance 42 of 21 October 1974, article 2), to remember the war dead and to seek lasting peace. This is a prefectural day, not a national holiday.

layers.process: Every visitor to the Kerama Islands pays JPY 100 (about A$0.90, RBA 30 October 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82). It is added to the ferry or plane fare. It is called the Beautiful Island Tax in the Zamami group and the Environment Support Tax on Tokashiki. The money goes to visitor facilities, plantings, public toilets and keeping harbours and beaches clean. The page was prepared in 2019, so the current amount and how it is collected are not confirmed here.
